hints.body: Write each option in if-then form, keeping the distinction between if, only if and if-and-only-if.

hints.body: Compare each implication with the contrapositive of every other one. Also separate the two directions inside each if-and-only-if.

hints.title: Check consistency
hints.body: After your logical eliminations, construct a simple function and test all the original statements against it.
hints.recap: A proposed sole truth must be compatible with every other listed statement being false.
hints.pitfall: Keep universal statements distinct from their truth at just one input.
hints.pause: Verify the remaining possibility on negative, zero and positive inputs.

recall.reminder: A proposed sole truth must be compatible with every other listed statement being false.

solution:
Rewrite the options as universal if-then rules:

  • A: x≥0⇒f(x)<0.
  • B: f(x)≥0⇒x<0.
  • C: x≥0⇒f(x)≥0.
  • D: x<0⇒f(x)<0.
  • E: f(x)≥0⇒x≥0.
  • F contains both x<0⇒f(x)≥0 and f(x)≥0⇒x<0.

A and B are contrapositives, so neither can be the sole true rule. D and E are another contrapositive pair, so neither can be the sole truth. F implies B, so F cannot be the sole truth either. Only C remains.

For consistency, take f(x)=|x|. C holds for all x≥0. A and B fail at x=0; D and E fail at x=−1; F fails at x=0. Thus exactly C can indeed be true.

Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Eliminate equivalent implications under an exactly-one premise
